public_rationale: SpaceX’s October 22, 2026 filing records completion of the Cursor merger on August 14, 2026, before the evaluation date [e1]. The completed acquisition satisfies the forecast’s acquisition branch and the contract’s early-resolution rule [e1]. Cursor announced a $2.3 billion Series D on November 13, 2025; this financing does not establish a durable independent alternative under the contract [e2].
limitations: The completed acquisition does not establish that continued independence was impossible or that acquisition was economically unavoidable.
The evidence does not establish that unsustainable unit economics caused the sale.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Cursor's only options are to die or be acquired.

statement.excerpt: Cursor, at this point, faces two options: die, or get acquired.

our_interpretation: Read as a categorical forecast that Cursor will ultimately close or be acquired.
“Die” means permanent business closure. “Get acquired” means a completed transfer of control, not discussions, an option, or an unsigned proposal.
No deadline is supplied. Temporary independent operation or another financing round does not by itself establish a durable third outcome.
The outcome assessment tests the predicted destination. It does not establish that acquisition was economically unavoidable.
criteria.support_condition: Cursor permanently closes or a buyer completes an acquisition transferring control of Cursor.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes a durable independent alternative, such as an independent public listing with viable ongoing operations or documented sustained self-financing independent operation.

evidence.explanation: The filing records a completed acquisition, satisfying one of the two forecast outcomes before the evaluation date.

Cursor announced further financing after the post. This qualifies any inference of immediate collapse or inability to attract capital, but does not establish sustainable independence or negate the later completed acquisition.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The filing confirms a completed acquisition, satisfying the contract’s rule that a completed acquisition conclusively supports the forecast.
